# 1 Chronicles Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 372r–372v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_004_page_001.jpg, 1CH_004_page_002.jpg

---

**4:1** The-sons of-Yehudah: Perets, Chetsron, and-Karmi, and-Chur, and-Shoval. **4:2** And-Re'ayah son of-Shoval fathered Yachat, and-Yachat fathered Achumai and-Lahad. These [are] the-families of-the-Tsor'ati.

**4:3** And-these [are] the-father of-Etam: Yizre'e'l, and-Yishma, and-Yidbash; and-the-name of-their-sister [was] Hatselelponi. **4:4** And-Penu'el [was] the-father of-Gedor, and-Ezer [was] the-father of-Chushah. These [are] the-sons of-Chur, the-firstborn of-Efratah, the-father of-Beit-Lechem.

**4:5** And-to-Ashchur, the-father of-Teqo'a, were two wives: Chel'ah and-Na'arah. **4:6** And-bore Na'arah to-him Achuzzam, and-Chefer, and-Teimeni, and-ha-Achashtari. These [were] the-sons of-Na'arah. **4:7** And-the-sons of-Chel'ah: Tseret, and-Tsochar, and-Etnan. **4:8** And-Qots fathered Anuv, and-ha-Tsovevah, and-the-families of-Achar'el son of-Harum.

**4:9** And-was Ya'bets more-honored [nikhbad] than-his-brothers. And-his-mother called his-name Ya'bets, saying [le'mor]: Because [ki] I-bore [him] in-pain [be-otseh]. **4:10** And-called Ya'bets to-the-God of-Yisra'el, saying [le'mor]: If [im] blessing [barekh] you-will-bless-me [tevarekheini], and-you-will-enlarge [vehirbita] my-border [gevuli], and-your-hand will-be [vehayetah yadekha] with-me [immi], and-you-will-do [ve'asita] from-evil [mera'ah] so-as-not [levilti] to-grieve-me [otsebi]! And-brought [vayyave] God [Elohim] that-which he-asked [et-asher sha'al].

**4:11** And-Keluv, brother of-Shuchah, fathered Mechir; he [was] the-father of-Eshton. **4:12** And-Eshton fathered Beit-Rafa, and-Paseach, and-Techinnah, father of-Ir-Nachash. These [are] the-men of-Rekhah.

**4:13** And-the-sons of-Qenaz: Otni'el and-Serayah. And-the-sons of-Otni'el: Chatat. **4:14** And-Me'onotai fathered Ofrah, and-Serayah fathered Yo'av, father of-Ge-Charashim [Valley of-Craftsmen], for craftsmen [charashim] they-were.

**4:15** And-the-sons of-Kalev son of-Yefunneh: Iru, Elah, and-Na'am. And-the-sons of-Elah: and-Qenaz. **4:16** And-the-sons of-Yehalel'el: Zif, and-Zifah, Tirya, and-Asar'el. **4:17** And-the-sons of-Ezrah: Yeter, and-Mered, and-Eifer, and-Yalon. And-she-conceived [vattehar] Miryam, and-Shammai, and-Yishbach, father of-Eshtemoa. **4:18** And-his-wife the-Yehudiyyah [the-Jewess] bore Yered, father of-Gedor, and-Chever, father of-Sokho, and-Yequti'el, father of-Zanoach. And-these [are] the-sons of-Bityah [daughter of-Pharaoh], whom Mered took.

**4:19** And-the-sons of-the-wife of-Hodiyyah, sister of-Nacham: the-father of-Qe'ilah the-Garmi, and-Eshtemoa the-Ma'akhati. **4:20** And-the-sons of-Shimon: Amnon, and-Rinnah, Ben-Chanan, and-Tilon. And-the-sons of-Yish'i: Zochet, and-Ben-Zochet.

**4:21** The-sons of-Shelah son of-Yehudah: Er, father of-Lekhah, and-La'dah, father of-Mareshah, and-the-families of-the-house of-the-working of-fine-linen [beit avodath ha-buts], of-the-house of-Ashbe'a, **4:22** and-Yoqim, and-the-men of-Kozeva, and-Yo'ash and-Saraf, who ruled [ba'alu] over-Mo'av, and-Yashubi-Lechem. And-the-records [ha-devarim] [are] ancient [atiqim]. **4:23** They [were] the-potters [ha-yotsrim] and-the-dwellers of-Neta'im and-Gederah; with-the-king in-his-work [bimla'khto] they-dwelt there.

**4:24** The-sons of-Shim'on: Nemu'el, and-Yamin, Yariv, Zerach, Sha'ul; **4:25** Shallum his-son, Mivsam his-son, Mishma his-son. **4:26** And-the-sons of-Mishma: Chammu'el his-son, Zakkur his-son, Shim'i his-son. **4:27** And-to-Shim'i [were] sixteen sons and-six daughters; and-to-his-brothers [were] not many sons, and-all their-families did-not-multiply to the-sons of-Yehudah.

**4:28** And-they-dwelt in-Be'er-Sheva, and-Moladah, and-Chatsar-Shu'al, **4:29** and-in-Bilhah, and-in-Etsem, and-in-Tolad, **4:30** and-in-Betu'el, and-in-Chormah, and-in-Tsiqlag, **4:31** and-in-Beit-Markavot, and-in-Chatsar-Susim, and-in-Beit-Bir'i, and-in-Sha'arayim. These [were] their-cities until the-reign [melokh] of-David. **4:32** And-their-villages [were] Etam, and-Ain, Rimmon, and-Tokhen, and-Ashan — five cities. **4:33** And-all their-villages that [were] around these cities, unto Ba'al. These [were] their-dwellings and-their-genealogical-registration [hityachsam] for-them.

**4:34** And-Meshovat, and-Yamlekh, and-Yoshah son of-Amatshyah, **4:35** and-Yo'el, and-Yehu son of-Yoshivyah son of-Serayah son of-Asi'el, **4:36** and-Elyo'enai, and-Ya'aqovah, and-Yeshochayah, and-Asayah, and-Adi'el, and-Yesimi'el, and-Venayah, **4:37** and-Ziza son of-Shif'i son of-Allon son of-Yedayah son of-Shimri son of-Shema'yah — **4:38** these who-came by-names [were] princes [nesi'im] in-their-families, and-the-house of-their-fathers broke-forth [paretsu] to-a-multitude [larov].

**4:39** And-they-went to-the-entrance of-Gedor, unto the-east of-the-valley, to-seek pasture [mir'eh] for-their-flocks. **4:40** And-they-found pasture fat [shemenah] and-good, and-the-land [was] broad of-hands [rachavat yadayim], and-quiet [shaqetah] and-secure [shalevet]; for from-Cham [were] those-dwelling there formerly [lefanim].

**4:41** And-came these the-written by-names in-the-days of-Chizkiyyahu, king of-Yehudah, and-they-struck their-tents and-the-Me'unim who were-found there, and-they-devoted-them [vayacharimum] unto this day, and-they-dwelt in-their-place; for pasture [mir'eh] [was] there for-their-flocks.

**4:42** And-from-them, from the-sons of-Shim'on, went to-Mount Se'ir five hundred men, and-Pelatyah, and-Ne'aryah, and-Refayah, and-Uzzi'el, sons of-Yish'i, at-their-head. **4:43** And-they-struck the-remnant [she'erit] of-the-escaped-ones [ha-peletah] of-Amaleq, and-they-dwelt there unto this day.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.9-10 — The Prayer of Jabez:** A remarkable interruption in the genealogical list. The name *Ya'bets* is a wordplay on *otseh* (pain). His prayer uses four petitions, each with the conjunction *vav*. The verb *otsebi* at the end echoes his name — he prays to be free of the pain his name declares.

**v.18 — Bithiah daughter of Pharaoh:** An Egyptian princess in a Judahite genealogy. The name *Bityah* means "daughter of YHWH" — a remarkable theological renaming of Pharaoh's daughter.

**v.22-23 — "the records are ancient":** The rare editorial comment *ha-devarim atiqim* suggests the Chronicler is working from old sources he can no longer fully interpret.

**v.40 — "broad of hands":** The idiom *rachavat yadayim* means "spacious" — literally "wide of hands," describing open territory.

*— EMET*
